Valve is Restricting Steam Trading Again To Combat Cheaters

Basically, this is that if a player gifts a game to someone who then gets VAC banned in it, you can no longer gift that game to anyone else. This feels like it would be more suited to punishing grey market sites. But what will stop them from making 1 account for each game, or stockpile as always, but for each gift out they instead give it to a new account as a middleman...?

When a user is caught cheating, their Steam account is banned from playing multi-player on secured servers. This creates an incentive for people who cheat to stockpile copies of games on one account and to gift them to low value accounts where they can continue cheating. In response to this problem, Steam no longer allows users to purchase copies of VAC or Game Ban enabled games to their inventory. Additionally, if an account has directly gifted a game to other players who have been VAC or permanently Game Banned, then that account will lose the ability to gift that game.

So instead of cheaters stockpiling copies of the game on one account (probably during a sale) to be traded to one of their alternate accounts later, cheaters will now either buy the game on multiple separate accounts, or possibly trade with someone who creates multiple accounts for the purpose of gifting VAC games. So basically they put a restriction on all steam users in order to solve a problem that they won't actually be solving at all, while creating more opportunity for scammers (ex: "u giev me ur itemz and I gift u CSGO its totally legit i swear"), thus generating even more support tickets and probably leading to the creation of thousands more throwaway steam accounts per week.
